messages:
maya: RFC follow-up: resume/activation handshake + telemetry for on-prem / air-gapped upgrades. Problem: nodes that lose power mid-apply often end up in an unclear state (blobs present but not activated). Proposal sketch: (1) activation nonce + signed activation attest stored in sealed manifest, (2) per-stage checkpoint file with compact summary (bloom + change-size), (3) ‘pending_activation’ state with remote-safe activate command, (4) short-lived recovery keys baked into the bundle for operator-initiated revert. Looking for feedback on UX and edge cases.

charlie: sounds good. two quick asks: include a monotonic apply_index so we can tell whether a restart progressed or rewound; and ensure the activation attest includes file fingerprints and node-local signature to prevent replay across nodes.

leah: agree on compactness. full hashes are prohibitive for large models. bloom + delta-size + optional sampling of file fingerprints should be enough for most triage. we can also emit a tiny, gzipped manifest snippet for the active component list.

samir: ops perspective: for the ‘remote activate’ flow, we need a safety check: controller must verify current on-disk fingerprints against the bundle snapshot before issuing activate. If mismatch, surface clear operator guidance (force vs reconcile). Also recommend retention: keep last 3 generations of artifacts and diffs by default.

maya: retention N=3 default fine; make it overridable per-cluster. For mismatch policy propose: (a) if fingerprints match => remote activation allowed; (b) if fingerprints partially match => require operator confirm; (c) if missing blobs => fail with explicit fetch-retry instructions.

nisha: small nit: how do we store the activation nonce and attest in air-gapped nodes? if we rely on sealed storage, we need migration story for disk replacement. Maybe store attest alongside checkpoint in the bundle dir and have agent re-seal into node-local keystore on first apply.

drew: +1 to node-local re-seal. We should also version the checkpoint schema so controller can evolve diagnostics without breaking old agents. I'll draft a proto with apply_index, stage_name, pending_activation boolean, bloom_base64, delta_bytes, sampled_fingerprints, and node_signature.

charlie: another edge-case: split-apply where a node downloads blobs but network to activation quorum is lost. We should expose an operator command `rw apply-resume --node <id> --verify` that will run local checks and optionally activate if verify succeeds. CLI should show a risk score computed from delta_size, sampled_mismatch_count, and time_since-last-checkpoint.

leah: for telemetry, we should emit minimal event series: apply.started, apply.checkpoint, apply.pending_activation, apply.activated, apply.rollback_requested, apply.rollback_completed. Each event should carry rollout_id and apply_index. Keep payload tiny.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging canary r-3432 kicked off; nodes=3; initial status=downloading.

samir: playbook snippet: if >1 node in replica set reports pending_activation for >10m and no progress -> controller pings ops channel, set a ‘quarantine’ tag, and prevent further rollouts until manual ack. auto-rollback only after operator timeout (30m) unless canary=false.

maya: consensus? do we like: conservative auto-rollback off by default for replica sets, but controller can be configured to auto-rollback for single-node clusters. And cross-region rollbacks always operator-confirm.

charlie: fine. one more: make sure rollout_id propagates into all logs and traces so Console can correlate client errors to rollout windows. That helped us diagnose last outage.

maya: great notes. action items: drew -> proto sketch for checkpoint schema; leah -> compressed-diff format + sampling policy; samir -> playbook quarantine + timeout text; nisha -> node-local seal migration doc. I'll update RFC with these and add CLI examples: `rw inspect-apply <node> --rollout r-3432` and `rw apply-resume --node <id> --force`. Tagging you all for review. :memo:
